To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
aggrecan, a major component of cartilage, activates the classical and the alternative pathway of the complement cascade.
aggrecan CLDs activate complement, and that this complement activation is attenuated by factor H binding to the CLD and CCP of aggrecan.

the C-type lectin of the aggrecan G3 domain activates complement via binding of C3 and C1q, and that this activation is counteracted by binding of factor H to the aggrecan C-type lectin and CCP domain.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of complement activation in the development of osteoarthritis and rheumatoid arthritis.
understanding how the complement system is regulated in joint disease.
understanding the mechanisms by which aggrecan G3 domain activates complement, and the role of the G3 in the pathophysiology of joint inflammation.

G3 CLD activates the classical pathway of the complement cascade and that this is regulated by binding of the complement inhibitor factor H.
the aggrecans C-type lectin activates complement, but that this is counteracted by the binding of factor H.
the G3 domain of aggrecan activates the classical pathway of complement via the CLD part of G3.

the CLD part of aggrecan G3 domain activates complement, but that the CCP part of G3 and the complement inhibitor factor H attenuate this activation.
